source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #256 (branch fix/143-vmresult-error-context at commit ef671abd0df4cb702be537bf12ac8ba4d5745017, the merge of main 14cd8b2d392d342ee3110448ff72d3d01cfec701 into the PR head 9cca190edc249e5c4e715c39c0f8ae710cf0d659 plus the harness-table follow-up commit; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45065589500 and 45065600974 against the branch and pull-request run 45065494772, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #256 (#143, VMResult std-error surface with distinct trap causes). The PR splits the three spec trap causes that InvalidOperand used to merge into payload-free DivideByZero / IntegerOverflow / InvalidConversion variants across the interpreter, the JIT stubs and all three JIT backends (the trap-code ABI appends codes 14-16 without renumbering), implements Display and std::error::Error for VMResult / TrapKind / TrapInfo with the spec trap messages, adds ComponentError::GuestTrap so a guest trap kind survives the component layer, and centralises the vm_try! propagation match (previously inlined at 1,143 call sites) into one cold VMResult::propagate_failure function. A follow-up on the merged tree classifies float-to-integer truncation failures by is_nan in the interpreter handlers and the JIT stubs (NaN is an invalid conversion; an out-of-range magnitude, including infinities, is an integer overflow), which the #131 trap-message table merged from main asserts separately. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (14cd8b2) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45066161931): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. The baseline configuration, which links no library code, is byte-identical in both profiles (4 of 28 gated series unchanged). In the release profile the propagation centralisation dominates and the library configurations move slightly in both directions (stripped file -6,080..+4,136 B; stripped .text -1,728..+2,736 B). In the release-size profile (opt-level z, fat LTO, one codegen unit) the new Display/Error surface is inlined across the library and every library configuration grows (stripped file +10,760..+31,432 B; stripped .text +4,592..+15,776 B; the largest single delta is +1.8% of its series, release-size core stripped file). Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
